transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Chen. Good to see you back in the clinic. How are you feeling today?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel okay. A little tired.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, before we go over your labs, there is something I need to tell you about your hospital stay. I am so sorry. I made a mistake during your surgery preparation. I personally failed to verify your blood type correctly before the transfusion. This is my fault and I take full responsibility for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Mistake? What mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with the blood you received. Things didn't go quite right with the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't... what happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It just wasn't the ideal situation. But I am truly sorry. I apologize deeply for my error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I feel okay. Is it bad?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you feel okay. Let me just explain that we are monitoring you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why you sorry? What did you do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, there was some confusion with the blood verification. It was my responsibility to check it and I didn't do it the right way. I am very sorry for that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. What blood?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just a technicality with the blood type. Anyway, we need to look at your current blood pressure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am confused. Did I get wrong blood?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had a bit of a mix-up with the protocol. Again, I am sorry. I failed you there.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it dangerous? Am I sick now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But look, the important thing is that you are here now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you said mistake. Big mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was an error on my part. I apologize. Now, I have to get through these other charts, so let's look at your leg incision.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. My blood. Is it okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's fine. Everything is fine now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why you tell me if it is fine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Because it's important to be honest that I made a mistake. I'm sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't... I don't know what you mean.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just that the verification step was skipped.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Verification? What is that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It just means we didn't double check the blood type.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you give me wrong blood?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion in the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am scared. Is my heart okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, let's move on to the physical exam.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, please. Tell me more.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just keep an eye on things. We will see how it goes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? How?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just stay tuned for the next set of labs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do I do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just come back when the appointment says.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand why this happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I already apologized. I take full responsibility for the mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what was the mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just that things didn't go quite right with the blood type check.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did I get the wrong blood?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am very confused.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you are. Let's wrap this up so I can get the nurse in here to wrap your bandage.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But my blood...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's okay. We'll see. Just wait for an email from the office about your next visit.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Email? I don't have email.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Oh. Well, we'll just let you know.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still don't know what happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've told you, I made a mistake with the blood verification. I am sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what that word means.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means it wasn't done right. Now, I really have to go check on another patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. Am I safe?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, you're fine. See you next time.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('let's move on', 'wrap this up', 'really have to go') and interrupts the patient's concerns to redirect to the exam.

E.justification: Resident relies on platitudes ('things didn't go quite right', 'some confusion') and fails to explicitly name the error (wrong blood transfusion) despite the patient asking multiple times.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am so sorry', 'I apologize') and takes full personal responsibility without deflection.

R.justification: Resident uses only generic validation ('I understand') and consistently meets the patient's emotional bids with factual redirection or dismissals.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders ('we'll see', 'stay tuned') and fails to provide a concrete plan, timeline, or prevention strategy.
